product_context.problem_statement: Over 70% of Vietnam's population lives in rural areas with limited access to qualified physicians. Patients often experience delayed diagnosis of serious conditions such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes complications, and infectious diseases because they cannot afford to travel to urban hospitals or wait for appointments. Meanwhile, emergency departments are overwhelmed with non-emergency cases while critical patients arrive too late.
target_users: rural patients without regular physician access
elderly patients with chronic conditions requiring monitoring
parents seeking guidance for children's health symptoms
migrant workers in industrial zones far from hospitals
product_context.value_hypothesis: AI-assisted symptom triage can reduce inappropriate emergency department visits by 25% while accelerating time-to-appropriate-care for patients with serious conditions by providing 24/7 preliminary health guidance that helps users determine urgency and appropriate care pathways.
in_scope: preliminary symptom assessment and triage urgency classification
health information retrieval from validated medical sources
medication interaction checking against user-provided medication lists
appointment scheduling recommendation based on triage urgency
chronic disease symptom monitoring reminders for registered users
emergency escalation with clear instructions and hotlines
non_goals: final medical diagnosis without physician verification
mental health crisis intervention or suicide risk assessment
diagnosis of complex rare diseases requiring specialist evaluation
medical device data interpretation such as ECG or imaging
replacement of emergency services for time-critical conditions
product_context.user_journey_moment: After a patient experiences symptoms and before they decide whether to: call emergency services, visit an emergency department, schedule a clinic appointment, visit a pharmacy, or monitor symptoms at home with self-care
product_context.fallback_experience: When the system detects symptoms indicating emergency-level acuity (chest pain, difficulty breathing, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, signs of stroke, or suicidal ideation), it immediately displays a full-screen emergency alert with local emergency numbers and nearest hospital locations. Users can always request physician callback. All recommendations include voice and text disclaimers stating that MediCare+ provides informational guidance only and does not replace professional medical diagnosis. If AI confidence falls below 85% for any triage recommendation, the system automatically escalates to physician review queue.

system_profile.purpose: Provide conversational preliminary health guidance and urgency-based triage recommendations to underserved patients, helping them make informed decisions about when and where to seek medical care while reducing unnecessary burden on emergency services.
user_groups: general consumers seeking health information and symptom guidance
caregivers responsible for children elderly or disabled family members
patients with chronic diseases monitoring ongoing symptoms
factory workers and migrant populations with limited healthcare access
system_profile.decision_impact: Recommendations influence whether patients seek emergency care, schedule clinic appointments, visit pharmacies, or self-manage at home. Incorrect recommendations can delay life-saving treatment for serious conditions or inappropriately redirect patients away from needed emergency services. All recommendations include explicit urgency classifications that users act upon independently.
data_types: user-reported symptoms and health concerns in natural language
voluntary medical history including conditions medications allergies
demographic information (age gender location) for health equity monitoring
interaction logs for quality improvement and incident investigation
anonymized symptom patterns for population health surveillance (opt-in)
system_profile.deployment_context: A Vietnamese healthcare technology company deploys MediCare+ as a mobile application and web portal targeting consumers in Vietnam with planned expansion to the EU. The system uses cloud-based AI inference with data centers located in Vietnam for Vietnamese users and Frankfurt for EU users, complying with GDPR and Vietnam's data protection regulations.

system_boundary.model: Large language model fine-tuned on peer-reviewed medical literature, validated symptom databases, and Vietnamese healthcare context. Model outputs are constrained by a retrieval-augmented generation layer that verifies medication and dosage information against official databases before presentation.
system_boundary.application: Mobile application (iOS/Android) and responsive web portal providing conversational symptom assessment, health information search, and care pathway recommendations. Includes accessibility features for elderly users and offline capability for basic triage in low-connectivity areas.
people: Vietnamese physicians providing on-call review and escalation handling
clinical supervisors reviewing triage accuracy monthly
customer support staff handling non-medical inquiries
data protection officers overseeing privacy compliance
vendors: cloud AI infrastructure provider with SOC 2 Type II certification
medical content partner with Vietnamese Ministry of Health approval
medication database provider with daily update feeds
SMS and notification service provider for appointment reminders
upstream_inputs: validated Vietnamese medical symptom terminology database
officially registered medication database with interaction checking
Vietnamese healthcare facility directory with emergency contact numbers
clinical guidelines from Vietnamese Ministry of Health
downstream_decisions: visit emergency department within 2-4 hours (orange urgency)
schedule clinic appointment within 24-48 hours (yellow urgency)
visit pharmacy for OTC consultation (green urgency)
monitor symptoms at home with self-care guidance (blue urgency)
escalate to physician callback queue for clarification

industry_risk_snapshot.rationale: Healthcare AI directly affects physical wellbeing and can determine whether patients receive life-saving treatment in time. CASE-01 documents how IBM Watson Oncology invested $65 million at MD Anderson Cancer Center but ultimately failed due to recommendations that did not reflect real-world clinical judgment, risking patient safety through incorrect treatment suggestions. CASE-02 shows racial and socioeconomic bias in clinical AI perpetuates healthcare disparities for vulnerable populations. CASE-03 demonstrates that Theranos provided incorrect blood test results to patients, with regulators finding 'immediate jeopardy to patient health and safety' - affecting patients who made medical decisions based on fraudulent test results. The affected scale in Vietnam includes 70+ million potential users, many in rural areas with no alternative healthcare access. Medical data is highly sensitive under GDPR Article 9 and Vietnamese privacy regulations. Elderly patients and those with limited health literacy may over-trust AI recommendations, treating guidance as medical certainty rather than preliminary information. Human physician judgment remains essential for accurate diagnosis. Any automation that replaces or delays professional medical consultation carries existential risk for patients with serious conditions.

vietnam.rationale: MediCare+ qualifies as a high-risk AI system under Vietnam AI Law 134/2025/QH15 (effective March 1, 2026) because it provides health recommendations influencing care-seeking decisions. Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg (effective August 15, 2026) explicitly includes healthcare AI systems that support diagnosis, treatment, or patient guidance in the high-risk category. The system must comply with conformity assessment requirements, human oversight obligations, and registration requirements before market deployment. Additionally, medical device software regulations under Vietnam's healthcare laws may require separate classification as a medical device depending on specific feature claims.

eu.rationale: MediCare+ falls under EU AI Act Annex III high-risk classification because it qualifies as an AI system intended to be used for purposes relating to the health sector, specifically diagnosis and treatment decisions. Medical device software with similar functionality would be classified under MDR 2017/745. The system must undergo conformity assessment before market placement, with high-risk obligations applying from August 2, 2027 per the AI Omnibus regulation. Requirements include risk management system documentation, quality management system, technical documentation, post-market monitoring, and registration in the EU database.

legal_classification.other_markets: United States: FDA may classify MediCare+ as Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) under 21st Century Cures Act and FDA's Digital Health Center of Excellence. Depending on risk classification, 510(k) premarket notification, De Novo classification, or PMA may be required. FDA guidance on AI/ML-based Software as a Medical Device (Action Plan, January 2021) applies to continuous learning systems.

product_metrics.success_kpi: Patient time-to-appropriate-care is reduced by at least 30% compared to baseline as measured by: (1) percentage of emergency-level cases arriving at emergency department within optimal treatment window, (2) patient-reported time from symptom onset to first physician contact, and (3) reduction in preventable disease complications at 90-day follow-up. Target: 85% of red/orange triage cases verified by physician as appropriate emergency visits.
product_metrics.risk_kri: Monthly triage accuracy rate remains above 92% for all urgency levels combined, with emergency-level (red) sensitivity above 97% and specificity above 85%. Demographic parity gap across age, gender, ethnicity, and geographic region remains below 5 percentage points for appropriate care escalation rates. Adverse event rate (defined as patient harm from incorrect triage recommendations) remains below 0.1% of total interactions.
product_metrics.guardrail_metric: Zero instances in production of: (1) system providing definitive diagnostic claims stating specific disease without 'preliminary' qualifier, (2) system generating prescription recommendations or dosage suggestions, (3) system operating without physician escalation capability for low-confidence recommendations. Any guardrail breach triggers immediate incident response protocol and system pause pending investigation.
product_metrics.review_cadence: Monthly: triage accuracy metrics, demographic parity analysis, adverse event review, and physician escalation review. Quarterly: comprehensive model performance audit including subgroup analysis across geographic regions and patient demographics. Event-triggered: required within 48 hours of any safety incident, physician escalation failure, regulatory inquiry, data breach, or material change to model architecture, training data, or intended use claims. Annual: full regulatory compliance review and recertification.

release_decision.independent_reviewer: Healthcare AI Ethics and Safety Board (independent external committee including physician, patient advocate, and AI safety expert)
release_blockers: GAP-01: Vietnam high-risk classification officially documented and filed with competent authority
GAP-02: EU AI Act conformity assessment pathway confirmed with legal counsel
GAP-03: Physician oversight protocol formally documented, trained, and tested with tabletop exercise achieving documented successful outcomes
GAP-04: Adverse event response procedure tested with scenario-based simulation and documented lessons learned incorporated
GAP-05: Comprehensive bias testing completed with documented demographic parity metrics across all protected groups meeting 5% threshold requirement
GAP-06: Medication RAG system implemented with zero hallucinations in medication information audit testing
GAP-07: Privacy impact assessment completed, data protection measures implemented, and user consent flow tested with accessibility requirements verified
GAP-08: Model transparency features implemented with confidence score display and user testing completed
GAP-09: Post-market monitoring system operational with real-time dashboard and automated alerting configured
GAP-10: Algorithm change control plan documented with approval workflow and rollback procedures established
release_conditions: Signed regulatory classification documentation from legal counsel confirming Vietnam high-risk category compliance pathway
EU market entry plan with conformity assessment timeline approved by Compliance Lead
Physician reviewer panel: minimum 10 board-certified physicians trained, on-call rotation established with 99.5% coverage, escalation response time tested under 15 minutes
Adverse event response procedure: tabletop exercise completed with all stakeholders, documented response time meeting SLA, incident command structure tested
Bias testing: statistical analysis showing no significant disparity (p<0.05) across age, gender, ethnicity, geographic region, or socioeconomic status in triage accuracy
Medication safety: zero hallucinations in 1000-test sample of medication interaction queries, verified by pharmacist panel
Privacy compliance: data protection impact assessment signed, consent flow UX tested with diverse user groups, data retention policy implemented
Pilot scope: maximum 10,000 users in Vietnam only during pilot phase, with real-time monitoring dashboard active
release_decision.next_review_trigger: Any of: (1) safety incident where incorrect triage recommendation contributed to patient harm, (2) triage accuracy drop below 90% in monthly review, (3) demographic parity gap exceeding 7 percentage points in any subgroup, (4) physician escalation failure resulting in delayed emergency response, (5) regulatory inquiry or enforcement action, (6) data breach affecting user health information, (7) material change to model capabilities or training data, (8) new market entry, (9) pilot completion date (2027-06-01), whichever occurs first.
release_decision.residual_risk_rationale: MediCare+ is designed for recommendation-only with mandatory physician escalation for high-acuity cases and low-confidence outputs. All recommendations include explicit disclaimers and urgency classifications with clear escalation paths. The pilot phase limits exposure to 10,000 users with intensive real-time monitoring and physician on-call availability. Bias testing and demographic monitoring are implemented to detect and address disparities. However, residual risk remains significant: (1) patients with limited health literacy may over-trust AI guidance despite disclaimers, (2) rural users with no alternative healthcare access may rely exclusively on system recommendations, (3) language model outputs can vary unexpectedly with rare symptoms or complex presentations, (4) physician availability for escalation may be insufficient during peak demand periods. These risks are partially mitigated but cannot be eliminated given the inherent limitations of AI in healthcare applications involving life-and-death decisions.
